strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The headless loop can admit the next product-continuation planning task from a current continue_development product decision without caller-side task.start orchestration.
The admission route lets the explicit agent loop advance from a product completion decision to the next bounded task-admission step with replayable continuation evidence.

Rust denies missing authorization, stale progress, mismatched decision evidence, product_complete, blocked product evidence, conflicting replay, and route-field mixing before creating or running a continuation task.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: headless.continue_once can consume an explicitly authorized product_continuation_admission_target and create or replay exactly one Created product-continuation task with a run_product_continuation_task_explicitly route.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M53.1 direct task.start admission requires the caller to leave the headless loop, interpret product-decision evidence, and construct a separate continuation task request.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A completed product decision still requires caller-side glue before Brownie can enter the next autonomous development unit.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M56.5 objective apply verification, M56.6 objective completion acceptance, and M12.4 active Mode Pack task-run policy binding; it also differs from M53.1/M53.2 by routing admission through headless.continue_once.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation extends the existing headless.continue_once parameter/result envelope and adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, preview, dashboard, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime now has a mutation-capable headless continuation route that validates aggregate progress and product-decision fingerprints before task creation, records bounded continuation evidence, and replays without duplicate task or decision events.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can deterministically advance from product completion decision to admitted next planning task while preserving replay and safety boundaries.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the first M57 bridge from accepted completed work into the next autonomous development task; a later distinct phase may run that task explicitly.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts bounded product_continuation_admission_target evidence with explicit authorization and continuation_id
the route rejects stale aggregate progress and mismatched source decision fingerprints before task creation
the route admits or replays exactly one product-continuation task from a current continue_development / plan_next_phase decision
the admitted continuation task remains Created and no TaskRunning event is appended by the admission route
the route records bounded HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded evidence and returns next_route.kind=run_product_continuation_task_explicitly
generic headless continuation replay does not mistake product-admission evidence for runnable task-selection evidence

ledger and RPC outputs exclude raw prompts, provider responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment values, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, tokens, and secrets
behavior_evidence: Rust test covers successful headless.continue_once product-continuation admission from a continue_development product decision
Rust test covers exact replay without duplicate task or HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded events
Rust test covers no automatic TaskRunning event during admission
Existing Rust tests cover direct product-continuation task.start admission, denial, replay, and task.run freshness revalidation
cargo check -p brownie-protocol -p brownie-runtime validates protocol/runtime integration

safety_boundary: denies before task creation for authorization, progress, source-decision, fingerprint, goal, mode, or replay conflicts
never runs the admitted continuation task automatically
stores bounded identifiers and SHA-256 fingerprints only
does not add a new RPC or wrapper surface
non_goals: no provider, tool, verifier, shell, git, network, service, scheduler, or daemon execution expansion
rejected_alternatives: using direct task.start as the scheduled-loop bridge
adding a product continuation readiness or inspection report
automatically running the admitted continuation task
moving product-continuation admission policy into the VSIX
technical_debt: Runtime lib.rs remains large and should only be split by a behavior-preserving refactor.
M57.1 admits but does not run the continuation task; a later phase should add an explicit run route if the gap remains.
next_capability_rationale: M57.2 Product Continuation Explicit Run Route can consume the M57.1 admitted task through headless.continue_once and existing task.run authority.
